minutes.headline: Cemetery Commission heard complaints about unkempt cemeteries and approved a headstone, flowers up to a cap; hedge quote and plan tabled.
minutes.summary: Residents and commissioners criticized the condition of the cemeteries before Memorial Day, and the DPW director described mowing, staffing and equipment steps now under way. The commission voted to approve an extra stone for a family, approved minutes, and authorized Lake View to do front-entrance flowers up to a stated cap. The hedge-trimming quote, open-lot mapping, lighting, and a detailed maintenance plan were put off to the June meeting.

public_comment.stated_role: resident, Highland Street; disabled Vietnam veteran
public_comment.topic: Cemeteries look unkempt, asked for a plan for mowing, said past staffing was leaner yet better, and asked about flags.
Agreed with prior speaker; said the Charter and bylaws are a mess and the split between day-to-day operations (DPW) and policy (commission) for cemeteries and parks must be resolved.
Asked why money seems short for needs yet two seasonal workers are hired, questioned what the superintendent has been doing, and offered to organize volunteers.

votes.motion: Allow the family to place an additional stone and move the current stone over at South Cemetery.
Have Lake View do the flowers for the North and South front cemeteries, up to a stated cap.

budget_items.what_was_said: The DPW director said his budget covers maintenance only, not upgrades such as turf restoration, and asked the commission to advocate for upgrade projects at budget time.
A resident recalled an allocation in the budget with a remaining balance and asked why money is short yet seasonal staff are hired.
Six landscapers were asked for prices; Lake View gave the best and is currently working, with two others available as backup.
A quote for trimming shrubs would come from commission funds; DPW director said he lacks the money until the new fiscal year in July. Tabled pending a description and timing.
Commission agreed it pays for the flowers, voted to cap the amount; DPW to handle watering.
Solar lights priced online were mentioned; concern about durability and installation cost; electricity run to flagpoles was costed as expensive.
Estimate from Leominster monument contractor for washing and repairing older stones, the figure was uncertain in the captions and in the master plan.
Former Gatsby Grounds owner suggested seeding and top dressing with a rough estimate.
A landscaper pilot and actual bill compared hours to mow North and South cemeteries.

decisions.decision: Chair and DPW director will meet first to begin a strategic/phased maintenance plan, then bring it back to the commission.
Hedge trimming quote tabled to June pending a description and timing check with Lake View.
Commission agreed no vote is needed for a family adding a memorial inscription for a relative buried elsewhere.
Open-lot mapping/printout for North Cemetery to be discussed at the June meeting.
DPW director to check with the town electrician and facilities director on flagpole lighting costs; chair to contact other cemeteries; return next meeting.
DPW director to consult Lake View and others on grub control, fertilizer and a calendar-based maintenance plan for the next meeting.

what_happened.line: The commission voted to let a family place an additional stone and move the current stone over at South Cemetery.
The commission voted to have Lake View do the front-entrance flowers at the North and South cemeteries, up to a stated cap.
Residents criticized the condition of the cemeteries ahead of Memorial Day, and the DPW director described mowing, staffing and equipment steps under way.
The Lake View hedge-trimming quote was tabled to June, pending a description and a timing check.
The chair and DPW director will meet first to start a phased maintenance plan, then bring it back to the commission.

why_it_matters: The DPW budget covers maintenance only, not upgrades such as turf restoration, so cemetery upgrades depend on the commission advocating for them at budget time.
Residents also raised the split between day-to-day operations (DPW) and policy (commission) as unresolved, which bears on who answers for cemetery upkeep.
watch_next: The June meeting: the hedge-trimming quote, North Cemetery open-lot mapping, flagpole lighting costs, and the maintenance plan are all due back.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on both non-procedural votes (the second headstone and the flowers) and on the tabled shrub-trimming quote. They differ mainly on the vote count and the attendee names. Our minutes omit the 3-0 tallies and the named commissioners, and treat the hedge, flagpole-lighting and mowing figures differently. The one thing to know: our "Mike" and "Dave" correspond to the official Michael Clark and David Dorren, and our unnamed Chair is Nancy Foss-Yasko.
